paper: Improved Upper Bounds for the Directed Flow-Cut Gap

numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Both edge and internal-vertex cut models; uniform n^(1/3+epsilon) rounding bound and advertised randomized polynomial algorithm.
Both models; factor n^epsilon sqrt(W), for every feasible fractional cut, uniformly in costs and W.
Fix c>=0; W^c n^o(1) implies n^(c/(1+c)+o(1)).
Uniform-weight unit-cost vertex bound transfers with polynomial n blowup and constant W blowup.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[See Theorems \ref{thm:edgetovert} and \ref{thm:vfgleefg}] \label{thm:edgetovertintro}
The directed edge and vertex flow-cut gaps are equivalent, up to factors of $O(\log n)$ in the number of nodes $n$ and $O(1)$ in the total weight $W$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Equivalence with O(n log n) versus 2n transformed vertices, constant versus exact W preservation.

numbered_statements.statement_tex: There is a randomized polynomial-time algorithm for minimum-cost edge or vertex multicut that achieves an approximation ratio of $\min\left\{\Ohat(n^{1/3}), \Ohat(W^{1/2})\right\}$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Minimum-cost multicut approximation; optimum fractional objective and executable polynomial-time rounding/optimization.

numbered_statements.statement_tex: The sparsest cut gap is at most $\min\left\{\Ohat(n^{1/3}), \Ohat(W^{1/2})\right\}$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Formal sparsest cut/concurrent-flow definitions and weight-preserving O(log n) transfer are indispensable.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
\label{cor:wldd}
Every $n$-node directed graph $G = (V, E, w)$ has a weak LDD with parameter $\texttt{LOSS} \le \min\left\{\Ohat(n^{1/3}), \Ohat(W^{1/2})\right\}$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Distribution supported on valid weak cuts; every item marginal <= LOSS*w/Delta; normalize W by Delta.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
\label{lem:vcr}
Let $G = (V, E)$ be an $n$-node directed graph and let $1 \le L \le n$.
Then in randomized polynomial time, one can construct a set of nodes $X \subseteq V$ that is an integral vertex cut for all node pairs $(a, b)$ at vertex-unweighted distance $\vdist_G(a, b) \ge L$,
and where with high probability $X$ has size
$$|X| \le \Ohat\left(\frac{n}{L}\right)^{3/2}.$$
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: 1<=L<=n; deterministic internal-cut validity; high-probability cardinality <=C_epsilon,A n^epsilon(n/L)^(3/2).
Weaker O((n/L)^2) version; independent of main theorem dependency graph.
For d in [h(u),h(v)), the level cut contains u or an internal vertex on every u-to-v path.

numbered_statements.statement_tex: Algorithm \ref{alg:main-alg} returns a correct integral cut $X$ (deterministically).
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Every returned cut hits internal vertices for every initial demand; endpoint d=1 needs an explicit closed-boundary argument.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Bound on Number of Epochs] \label{lem:numepochs}
The number of epochs in the algorithm is at most $O\left(\frac{\log n}{\log \log n}\right)$.
dependencies: mass decreases by log n at a switch
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Finite bound for n sufficiently large; one possible final zero-mass epoch; retained old mass need not be zero merely because demands are already cut.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Cost of $i$-Round Epoch] \label{lem:epochcost}
For any epoch and any positive integer $i$, the expected number of new nodes added to $X$ during the first $i$ rounds of the epoch is at most
$$\mass\left(\{w_{s, t}\}\right) \cdot \left( \frac{i}{|P|}\right)$$
where $\mass, |P|$ are measured at the beginning of the epoch.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Given start mass M0 and pair count p0>0, expected new vertices in first i stopped rounds <=M0*i/p0.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Bound on Rounds per Epoch] \label{lem:roundbound}
With high probability, every epoch will terminate within at most
$$\Ohat\left(\frac{|P| \cdot n^{3/2}}{\mass\left(\{w_{s, t}\}\right) \cdot L^{3/2}}\right)$$
rounds of the main loop, where $\mass$ and $|P|$ are measured at the beginning of the epoch.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: High-probability rounds <=C n^epsilon p0(n/L)^(3/2)/M0, with M0 measured at epoch start; printed proof uses current mass instead.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
\label{lem:valub}
With high probability,\footnote{As usual, ``with high probability'' means probability at least $1 - \frac{1}{n^C}$, where the constant $C$ may be pushed arbitrarily high by choice of high enough implicit constants.} for all pairs of nodes $(u, v)$ with $\val(u,v) > 0$, if 
$$\Omega\left( \frac{|P|}{\val(u, v)} \cdot \log n \right)$$
rounds of the epoch pass then there will no longer be a $u \leadsto v$ path in $G \setminus X$.
(This is either because $X$ is a cut for $(u, v)$, or because $u \in X$.
The value of $|P|$ is measured at the start of the epoch.)
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Freeze all weights and P0; joint event epoch survives i and pair survives has probability <=exp(-i*val0/p0).

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Lower Bound on $\val$] \label{lem:vallb}
In any round of an epoch, there exists a pair of nodes $(u, v)$ with
$$\val(u, v) \ge \mass\left(\{w_{s, t}\}\right) \cdot \Omegahat\left(\frac{L}{n}\right)^{3/2}.$$
and where there exists a $u \leadsto v$ path in $G \setminus X$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Current positive mass M implies a reachable pair in G minus X with val>=M(L/n)^(3/2)/K(n). Literal endpoint counterexample affects this pipeline.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Path System Witness Lemma]\label{lem:pathwitness}
At the beginning of each round, there exists a path system $R = (V, \Pi)$ (over the same vertex set as $G$), as well as a partition of the paths $\Pi$ into (possibly empty) parts
$$\Pi = \bigcup \limits_{(s, t) \in P} \Pi_{s, t},$$
with all of the following properties:

\begin{enumerate}
\item For each part $\Pi_{s, t}$, the paths in $\Pi_{s, t}$ are pairwise vertex-disjoint.

\item For any path $\pi$ in a part $\Pi_{s, t}$, $\pi$ is a not-necessarily-contiguous vertex subsequence of some $s \leadsto t$ path in $G \setminus X$.
Moreover, letting the vertex sequence be $\pi = (v_0, \dots, v_k)$, we have $\frac{L}{\lambda} \le k \le L$ for some $\lambda = n^{o(1)}$, and for each index $i$ we have
$$\vdist_{s, t}(s, v_i) + \frac{1}{L} \le \vdist_{s, t}(s, v_{i+1}),$$
and also $\vdist_{s, t}(s, v_k) \le 1$.

\item $|\Pi| \ge \Omegahat\left(\mass\left(\{w_{s, t}\}\right)\right)$
\end{enumerate}
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Demand-labelled vertex-disjoint subsequences, length L/lambda<=k<=L, distance increments>=1/L, final distance<=1, and |Pi|>=M/K. False as printed; see COUNTEREXAMPLES.md.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Base Path] \label{lem:basepath}
Let $R$ be a path system as in Lemma \ref{lem:pathwitness}, and let $d$ be the average of $\texttt{deg}_{\Pi}(v)$ over its nodes.
Then there exists a path $\pi_b \in \Pi$ with the property that
$$\sum \limits_{v \in \pi_b} \texttt{suffdeg}_{\Pi}(v) \ge \frac{L d}{\lambda}.$$
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Nonempty path family; average degree d; base suffix-incidence >=Ld/lambda with explicitly enlarged lambda and minimum length.
Reachability-preserving shortcut pairs S of size O(L log n); every reachable base-path pair has <=2 hops; at most O(log n) mediators per first endpoint.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
\label{lem:valsplit}
If an edge $e \in S$ is charged for $\alpha$ total points of value throughout the charging scheme, then $\val(e) \ge \frac{\alpha}{2}$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Total charge alpha to a directed pair implies val>=alpha/2; each demand contributes at most twice.
At least Ld/(2lambda) deletions imply reachable e in S with val>=sigma*d/(L*K(n)).
At most Ld/(2lambda) deletions imply reachable e with val>=L^2*d/(sigma*n*K(n)); reachability is implicit in statement but used later.
val_s,t(u,x)<=val_s,t(u,v)+val_s,t(v,x), including unreachable distances and reversed interval endpoints.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Path System Structure] \label{lem:pathstructure}
If the charging scheme halts within $\le \frac{Ld}{2\lambda}$ rounds, then once it halts, there exists a node $u \in V$ and a subset of paths $Q \subseteq \Pi$ of size
$$|Q| \ge \Omegahat\left(\frac{L^2d}{\sigma n}\right)$$
where all paths $q \in Q$ have $u \in \texttt{prefix}(q)$, and also $\texttt{suffix}(q)$ intersects $\pi_b$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Early halting yields a vertex u and Q of size >=L^2*d/(sigma*n*K(n)), sharing a prefix vertex and meeting the base path in each suffix.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Lower Bound on Path Lengths]
For any path $\pi''' = (v_0, \dots, v_k)$ added to a part $\Pi_{s, t}$, we have $k \ge \Omegahat(L)$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Selected length k>=L/K(n); printed deleted-weight proof conflates removal of used vertices with later thinning.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[System Size]
The final size of the path system satisfies $|\Pi| \ge \Omegahat\left(\sum \limits_{(s, t) \in P} w_{s, t}(V \setminus X)\right)$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: |Pi|>=M/K(n); endpoint counterexample defeats claimed candidate feasibility.

numbered_statements.statement_tex: $\vufg(n, W) \le O\left(\vuufg\left(O(n), O(W)\right)\right)$
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: At most 2n vertices, total weight <=2W, output size <=2W times transformed gap; max(1,ceil(...)) and W=0 case needed.

numbered_statements.statement_tex: $\vfg(n, W) \le O(\vufg(O(n^2), O(W)))$
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: O(n^2) vertices and O(W) total weight; printed contraction loses demand endpoints. See counterexample.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
\label{thm:edgetovert}
$\efg(n, W) \le O\left(\vfg\left(O(n \log n), O(W)\right)\right)$
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: O(n log n) vertices, W'<=4W and objective'<=4objective after clipping; lifting all transformed paths must be proved.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
\label{thm:vfgleefg}
$\vfg(n, W) \le \efg(O(n), W)$
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Exactly 2n vertices, W'=W; high-cost connector exclusion and endpoint-out/endpoint-in lift.

numbered_statements.statement_tex:
[Folklore] \label{thm:vfgself}
If $\vfg(n, W) \le W^{c+o(1)}$ for some constant $c$, then $\vfg(n, W) \le n^{\frac{c}{1+c} + o(1)}$.
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: For fixed c>=0 use threshold n^(-c/(1+c))/4; endpoint-safe residual argument; explicit subpolynomial factors.

numbered_statements.statement_tex: There is a weak LDD for vertex cuts with loss parameter $\Oish(\vfg(n, W))$, and a weak LDD for edge cuts with loss parameter $\Oish(\efg(n, W))$.
numbered_statements.role: generalized background reduction with new proof
numbered_statements.formal_contract_note: Edge and vertex weak LDDs from rounding bounds; printed update fails. A common learning-rate replacement is proposed in COUNTEREXAMPLES.md.

numbered_definitions.statement_tex:
[$\mass$ function]
At any point in the algorithm, we define
$$\mass\left(\{w_{s, t}\}\right) := \sum \limits_{(s, t) \in P} \sum \limits_{v \in V \setminus X} w_{s, t}(v).$$

[$\val$ function]
    In an epoch, for a pair of nodes $(u, v)$ and a demand pair $(s, t) \in P$, we define
    $$\val_{s, t}(u, v) := \Pr_{d \sim [0, 1]}\bigg[ d \in \left[\vdist_{s, t}(s, u), \vdist_{s, t}(s, v)\right]\bigg]$$
    and
    $$\val(u, v) := \sum \limits_{(s, t) \in P} \val_{s, t}(u, v).$$

[Path Prefixes, Suffixes, Degrees]
The prefix, suffix of a path $\pi \in \Pi$ are the contiguous subpaths respectively consisting of the first, last $\lfloor |\pi|/4 \rfloor$ nodes of $\pi$.
For a node $v$, we write $\texttt{deg}_{\Pi}(v)$ for the number of paths in $\Pi$ that contain $v$, and we write $\texttt{suffdeg}_{\Pi}(v)$ for the number of paths in $\Pi$ that contain $v$ in their suffix.
